subject: Seeking Guidance: Implementing Mediation Models in SAM Approach

messages.author: 4cc1c790c0e6f292
messages.subject: Seeking Guidance: Implementing Mediation Models in SAM Approach
parts:
Dear All,

I hope this email finds you well.

In traditional SEM, mediation models are straightforward and well-documented (for reference, see the lavaan tutorial: https://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/mediation.html).

Given my smaller sample size (N = 686), I’m exploring the possibility of running my mediation analysis within the Structural After Measurement (SAM) approach instead. However, I’m currently seeking guidance on how to adapt or implement a mediation model using the SAM methodology.

Here is my hypothesis (adapted from SEM):

  • Ant ~ a1 * ACE
  • Dis ~ a2 * ACE
  • ASB ~ b1 * Ant
  • ASB ~ b2 * Dis
  • ind1 := a1 * b1
  • ind2 := a2 * b2

Where:

  • Ant = Antagonism
  • Dis = Disinhibition
  • ACE = Adverse Childhood Experiences
  • ASB = Antisocial Behavior

If you’ve worked on something similar or have insights/resources for implementing a mediation model using SAM, I would greatly appreciate your advice or recommendations!

Thank you in advance for your time and support.

Best regards,
Maximilian

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Seeking Guidance: Implementing Mediation Models in SAM Approach
parts:
Can we assume that Ant/Dis/ACE/ASB are latent variables measured by
indicators?

In that case, there is no difference between SEM and SAM when it comes
to mediation analysis. The syntax is the same.

If you have two groups, then you should vectorize your labels. So
instead of

you should write

Ant ~ c(a1.g1, a1.g2) * ACE

where 'g1' and 'g2' stands for the first and second group respectively.
Then, in a follow up model, you can replace this by

Ant ~ c(a1, a1) * ACE

where you use the same label for both groups. Then you will constrain
this coefficient to be same across the groups.

Yves.

messages.author: 4cc1c790c0e6f292
messages.subject: Re: Seeking Guidance: Implementing Mediation Models in SAM Approach
parts:
Dear Yves,

Thank you very much for your helpful feedback! I’m sorry for not providing enough details earlier. To clarify, the variables I mentioned are all latent variables measured by indicators and at first I fitted each measurement model.

I followed your recommendations, and everything worked well — thank you again! I now have a couple of follow-up questions as I continue analyzing my results:

  1. Global vs. Local SAM Fit Indices
    I used the global SAM method to obtain pseudo-fit indices, as I understood this is the appropriate approach (hopefully, I interpreted it correctly!). When using the global SAM method, the fit indices across groups don’t differ much, which seems reasonable.

     

    However, I noticed that the fit indices from the local SAM method differ significantly compared to the global SAM fit indices. Do you know why this might be the case? Is it expected for global and local SAM to produce such different results?

  2. Constraining the Model Across Groups
    Did I understand correctly that you would recommend not constraining the model across groups using e.g. group.equal = c("loadings", "intercepts", "regressions")? 

  3. Interaction Effects Between Groups and Predictors
    Even if the fit indices are comparable between the models, regression coefficients differ between the groups. 

    Would you recommend explicitly testing for an interaction effect between group membership and the predictor variable? Or would this interaction essentially lead us back to the same group-specific effects already identified in the model?

I appreciate your patience and guidance as I work through these questions. Thank you again for your help!

Best regards,
Maximilian

parts:
Dear Group,

after the help of Yves I could correct the model and rewrite it. I also adjusted the measurment model of my internalizing factor, which is now 3 factors (Anxiety, Depression, Stress from DASS-21, which is in line with theory and prior analyses) and now the fit indices of LSAM seems alright. 

Because it is a mediation model I specified indirect and total effects.

I post here the structural model; all variables have latent indicators. All of them have been tested separately as recommended by SAM approach. 

My problem is: I don't get the total effects for Group 2 (I have two groups). 

I reduced the model to find the mistake. In the original model has more latent variables. 

# Part 1: ACE predicting latent variables (mediators)
Ant ~ c(a1.g1, a1.g2) * ACE    # a-path (X → M)

# Part 2: Mediators predicting outcomes
ASB ~ c(b1.g1, b1.g2) * Ant    # b-path (M → Y)
ASB ~ c(c1.g1, c1.g2) * ACE     # Direct effect (X → Y)

# Indirect effects
indirect_ASB_g1 := c1.g1 * b1.g1   # Indirect effect through mediator
indirect_ASB_g2 := c1.g2 * b1.g2   

# Total effects
total_ASB_g1 := c1.g1 + indirect_ASB_g1   # Total effect on ASB
total_ASB_g2 := c1.g2 + indirect_ASB_g2   

The output looks like this:
Group 1 [Prison]:

Regressions:
                   Estimate  Std.Err  z-value  P(>|z|)
  Ant ~                                              
    ACE     (a1.1)    0.035    0.018    1.943    0.052
  ASB ~                                              
    Ant     (b1.1)    1.155    0.438    2.638    0.008
    ACE     (c1.1)    0.037    0.037    0.999    0.318

Group 2 [Community]:

Regressions:
                   Estimate  Std.Err  z-value  P(>|z|)
  Ant ~                                              
    ACE     (a1.2)    0.066    0.016    4.088    0.000
  ASB ~                                              
    Ant     (b1.2)    0.672    0.102    6.580    0.000
    ACE     (c1.2)    0.128    0.031    4.138    0.000

Defined Parameters:
                   Estimate  Std.Err  z-value  P(>|z|)
    indirct_ASB_g1    0.043    0.048    0.888    0.375
    indirct_ASB_g2    0.086    0.027    3.165    0.002
    total_ASB_g1      0.080    0.084    0.949    0.342

I have checked the model throughout with:

parameterEstimates(LSAM_EPA.SF_Original_Unconstrained2, standardized = TRUE)
lavInspect(LSAM_EPA.SF_Original_Unconstrained2, "user")

but total_ASB_g1 does not appear. 

I have specified the model per group only. Then total_ASB does not appear too — in both groups. If I constrain the regressions across over both it does appear.

If I fit the model as "sem" then I get both total_ASB parameters; so is this maybe a problem of "sam"?

What could be the problem/? 

I dont get errors.
